newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally on Wall Street gains.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally on Wall Street gains.

text.p: Mexican shares recovered from a mid-session lull to close sharply up for the second day in a row on Friday in the wake of a revival on Wall Street, traders said.
"Although it was a very speculative market, it did respond to advances by the Dow Jones," said Rodolfo Campuzano, an analyst at the Invex brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 51.46 points, or 1.35 percent, at 3,873.38.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, meanwhile, closed up 32.92 points to 7,169.54.
Trading volume was lacklustre at 70.6 million shares.
"The Dow (Jones) rally today and falling U.S. long bond yields were a great help. I feel we can keep climbing, as we have lagged a long way behind the Dow," a desk trader said.
"Economic figures yesterday were good and people took notice of them today, prompted by the Dow," he added.
"After mid-session the market had managed to purge such sales as there were and then orders to buy flooded in," a floor trader said. "The short-term outlook is good."
Dealers said that Telmex led the rally, buoyed by its ADRs and news it had obtained a $1 billion syndicated loan.

The telecomms firm's L class shares, which accounted for 17 percent of all shares traded, gained 30 centavos to 16.80 pesos, while its ADRs ended up 1/2 at 42-1/8. Financial group Bancomer was the most
traded loser, off one centavo to 2.84 centavos, after a volatile day in which dealers said it acted like a weather vane for the U.S. long bond.

The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 17/32 in late trade to yield 6.89 percent, after zigzagging through the session. Higher yields earlier in the day spurred fears of rises in domestic rates that unsettled investors concerned about the negative impact on past-due loans, dealers said.
On the broad market, of 109 stocks traded, gains outnumbered losses 60 to 24.

Troubled Mexican conglomerate Sidek topped the percentage gainers' list for the third day, up six centavos to 48 centavos, closely followed by its tourism subsidiary Situr, up two centavos to 36 centavos.
"The share has been recovering swiftly, they say there will be good news for its pending debt restructur," a trader said.
Hotel operator Posadas was also near the top of the gainers' list, up 25 centavos to 3.85 pesos on speculation the firm was to build a hotel on the site of a Mexico City racetrack, traders said.
